cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Players experience motion sickness from close camera angles, lack online multiplayer, find keyboard controls clumsy, and report rushed narrative pacing with excessive walking and missing character creators.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game's camera positioning is too close and causes motion sickness.

citations.review_text: Disappointing. The split screen sucks, made a bad choice not using online coop with this one. Took us ages to connect another controller, kept bugging out. Played for 20 mins in total, the rest of the playtime is us dealing with bugs and connectivity issues. The split screen is so frustrating, the game is so close to the camera you feel way too close to the character, camera angles and movement feels weird and dizzy inducing. The general gameplay feels slow and clunky. I'm glad i got this on a huge sale because I didnt loose much in terms of money, but i did loose a lot of sanity.

Visually beautiful upgrade to a classic series of games, all the usual fun of puzzles, comedy, and most of all collecting studs. Unfortunately the camera is very close to your character when using 16:9 display, and the games automatic camera movement is pretty awful. This combined with no FOV options or camera zoom preferences makes it an instant motion sickness trigger. I see many reviews with a similar story. It's something I'd have never considered for a game in this genre but unfortunately unplayable for me in this state.

I really want to like this game and play all of it but i can't play more than a few minutes at a time without getting very very motion sick. 
I'm not the only one, I've tried playing this my family members on the couch and the major complaint is very quickly does motion sickness set in. Tried playing on a monitor, a tv and a handheld. none of which have helped the motion sickness. 
Looks atleast a 100 hour game just to get all the achievements and unlock all the things. 
Wish i could recommend it. Would greatly appreciate if Accessibility settings were added (impossible at this point i know)
The camera use on PC is so atrocious it ended up giving me a massive headache that didn't go away for hours. Had to refund as it was unplayable for me.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game lacks online multiplayer and restricts cooperative play to split-screen or remote play.

citations.review_text:
The co-op sucks because of the lack of a fixed camera like the older games. It also forces you to use a vertical split screen which makes the FOV very limited. Also, I had to restart the Episode 1 Tatooine mission because half of the characters were invisible and could not be controlled.
Also, the performance is absolutely abysmal in co-op. Just play the originals, the sequel trilogy sucks anyways.
only reason i dont recommend the game is because it doesnt have online multiplayer despite releasing in 2022

Bought two copies to play with my girlfriend. This game is tagged as multiplayer AND Co-op. Multiplayer implies two different players with two different copies can play together. Unfortunately, that's not possible with this game. This game is strictly Co-op, meaning one person with one copy can hook up a second controller and play split screen. Why does it even have the misleading multiplayer tag? What's worse is that Steam wouldn't even refund because I took 3 weeks to request refund instead of two... Honestly pretty disappointed with Steam as a whole after this, and especially with Lego Star Wars. I can't recommend this game.

I wanted to like this game, but of the three times I've tried it, I just can't get into it. I've loved previous LEGO games, But as they've gotten more complex, they also somehow become overwhelming and underwhelming at the same time. Overwhelming because there's just an endless amount of collectables, "secrets", huge open hubs with many small side missions, and a large roster of characters. Underwhelming because it just feels like everything lacks focus. And in 2022, there's no excuse for not having online multiplayer/co-op. Couch co-op is great, but for goodness sakes at least have the option to play on two separate devices/screens.

Disappointing. The split screen sucks, made a bad choice not using online coop with this one. Took us ages to connect another controller, kept bugging out. Played for 20 mins in total, the rest of the playtime is us dealing with bugs and connectivity issues. The split screen is so frustrating, the game is so close to the camera you feel way too close to the character, camera angles and movement feels weird and dizzy inducing. The general gameplay feels slow and clunky. I'm glad i got this on a huge sale because I didnt loose much in terms of money, but i did loose a lot of sanity.

Trash, Me and my Girlfriend both bought it, no multiplayer, only remote play which splits both screens, and that would be fine and all we just wanna play a game we both paid 60 bucks for well, even remote play doesn't work, waited a year and still nothing, we wanted to play this game but couldn't get it to work no matter how hard we tried, also didn't work with my controller very well. if you are interested in this don't bother unless you want to play alone.

This game needs a new user-defined tag. This game does NOT include Multiplayer at all, and does not feature an easy accessible CO-OP.

 You need to use remote play, or some other external downloaded program. Even then one player MUST require a controller. 
You CANNOT play with TWO KEYBOARDS + MICE. ONLY ONE KEYBOARD + MOUSE player and ONE CONTROLLER player.

 Game might be good as a solo experience but Multiplayer/Co-op was the entire reason I bought this game.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that mouse and keyboard controls feel clunky and poorly implemented, including unsupportive menu navigation.

citations.review_text:
Completed 100% on PS5 so ignore the low play time. If you get this game expecting it to be like the 2007 release, you're going to be extremely disappointed. That aside, once you get past the awful voice acting it's a pretty good game. A rare W for Disney with Star Wars. 

Mouse and Keyboard controls are horrendous though and the crappy Dualsense implementation on PC doesn't help much.
playing this on a computer with keyboard is not something i would recommend and the controls are just bad. i don't want to keep playing this game since there are better lego star wars games.

The menu system has to be navigated by keyboard. There is no mouse support for the menu system at all.  There's a store page before the main menu that it doesn't tell you how to get out of (it's space, I had to look it up via google). It's obvious that they did the bare minimum for mouse/keyboard to get it functional. Overall that makes it a really bad port as far as I'm concerned.

Also, the performance is absolutely abysmal in co-op. Just play the originals, the sequel trilogy sucks anyways.

Played for 20 mins in total, the rest of the playtime is us dealing with bugs and connectivity issues. The split screen is so frustrating, the game is so close to the camera you feel way too close to the character, camera angles and movement feels weird and dizzy inducing. The general gameplay feels slow and clunky. I'm glad i got this on a huge sale because I didnt loose much in terms of money, but i did loose a lot of sanity.

Has some technical issues caused by bad development (having to restart the game after moving the game to a different screen and then changing the resolution to 4K) but the biggest issue is how far Lego games have fallen. 

The game is WAY too easy even after disabling the baby mode options. Lego games have always been 3+ but still offered a challenge but this is a new low that my 4 month kitten could play this in her sleep (not even a joke, you cant die since jedi auto deflect enemy fire)! 

The levels are super compressed compared to what the original game offered. You are rushed through the episodes rather than episodes having chapters you progress through and unlock things through individual levels. 

Co-op feels claustrophobic since you can no longer share the same screen and things that used to be cut scenes are now open world trash however I don't care too much about that last point. 

I also hate episodes 7-9 in general so wasn't going to buy this until I saw it dropped to £3 so I though why not and oh boy it was a waste of time!

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Players report short campaign levels with repetitive puzzles, missing character customization features, and technical issues including crashes and save file corruption, contrasted with praise for the massive open world and extensive character roster.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the campaign levels are very short, featuring repetitive puzzles and a heavy emphasis on walking and talking sequences.

citations.review_text:
This one's really complicated. It's a game I really, *really* wanted to like. I even pre-ordered it for my Switch. And in some ways, this game does live up to expectations. The character roster is massive and expansive, all 9 saga films in one game, a revamped combat system with a big focus on stringing together fun lil combos. But it's also immensely disappointing in other ways. Most of the story mode gameplay is walking from point a to point b while characters talk. Missions range from decent to incredibly short and disappointing. The level selection itself is very weird and massive setpieces are excluded from the game or included as very brief cutscenes. Did you guys notice that every single lightsaber duel works the exact same, give or take a Force Lightning attack for the people who use that? 

I think the issue is that there's just too much of this game. It's real easy to hop on and grind Kyber Bricks for hours in the open worlds, but they're not particularly challenging or interesting and there's, might I add, ONE THOUSAND AND TWO HUNDRED of them to collect. This is on top of the Minikits, and the 300 character large roster (that's like a quarter costumes for main characters), and the 80 or so ships (speaking of this, why is the Republic Gunship not in this game??) and the 19 cheat code collectibles. I know it's weird to expect any level of challenge from a LEGO game, they're all pretty easy, but none of them are *this* dense and none of them ask you to do the same 6 puzzles and 3 retrieval missions slightly reshuffled nearly as many times as this game does. 

Also, I'm a fully grown ass adult and this is a baby game meant for babies. I'm sure this game is awesome if you're a kid growing up with it, and I fully admit my love for the original LEGO Star Wars games is hugely driven by nostalgia, but it doesn't make this one any less disappointing or dull to play.

It's a very pretty Star Wars game, graphics has come a long way since the original and prequel lego games. The game itself is also great, unfortunately I am a little too old to enjoy it as much as I know I would have 15-18 years ago. 

There is a lot of exploration and things to discover. However there is a caveat that there is also a lot of slop, especially side missions and even the main episodes. For example running from Point A to B with little gameplay substance or traversing through planets (i.e., loading screens) just to talk to a NPC or pick something up. However, from my experience there is the occasional gem or puzzle that can keep things somewhat interesting.

There is also a TON of collectables, particularly 1200 Kyber Bricks. At the point of this review, I have only collected 323 of them, however there is no way I will collect all 1200 scattered across the planets. I have collected some things that I thought would somewhat satisfy my collecting itch, such as datacards and true jedi levels (like the original lego games), however that is as far as I'm willing to go.

The menu UI is also too messy and needed to be a lot simpler as it feels overwhelming at the beginning. Traversing through the map with the keyboard was also a shocker to get the cursor to adjust onto a location/collectable. 

Overall fun game to play casually, and will definitely be even more fun for kids,

So SO much to do and collect and explore, there is absolutely no lack of content, you'll always be busy doing something
That being said how do you make every bit of the game either boring or feel like filler
Campaign has a ton of levels but every level is like 5 minutes long and it feels like you're forced to speedrun the game
But then free play and open world hits... 1200+ collectibles????
With THIS MUCH ♥♥♥♥ to collect, nothing stands out and every "puzzle" feels like a chore if you wish to 100%
And why does almost every side quest require you to travel to 3 other planets on average
Because of how much you'll be going back and forth between planets, this game becomes a loading screen simulator

The game also seems to get buggier the longer you play it??
Literally new type of bug gets introduced every few hours
Sound desyncing, infinitely respawning in the void, being unable to accept some side quests until you reload the area, the lock-on in space fights just not existing sometimes, game crashes, in some areas you have a 50% chance for the game to eat your jump input, General Grievous (yea just him entirely), random hard lag for long periods of time until the game decides that it had enough and crashes again, in the level where you're supposed to destroy tie fighters with the millennium falcon when they fly in front of you... they can just decide to stay behind you for as long as they want leading to this 3 minute level taking about 15 minutes
And these are all the bugs I remember from the top of my head, if I documented every single bug I experienced, it would be longer than his review tenfold

Congrats, you made a 50 hour long game feel like filler... and it would've been longer if I haven't played the entire game with a friend

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game lacks features present in previous titles, notably the character customizer.

citations.review_text: while i love star wars, the fact that there is (as of playing the game, not as of right now) no character creator soured the experience for me quite a bit

Not bad, but it's missing features from past games. The character customizer is a big one, but the one I really miss is being able to choke/zap anyone with the Sith characters. Now you can only torture villain characters.

The open worlds are cool too, but I do miss the feeling of casually picking bar fights with characters from different eras in Dexter's Diner and the Mos Eisley Cantina.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the open world as massive and detailed, featuring an extensive roster of characters and ships from across the nine films.

citations.review_text: This game is massive. It's full of content & exploration possibilities. The open world in the game is huge, no other LEGO game operated with this big enviroment. Seems like developers wanted to show us everything about the Star Wars universe, and they've made a pretty well job. On the other hand, the levels feel very short, certain events happening out of the missions without any replay opportunity. Comparsion with the classic LEGO Star Wars games is inavoidable in this case, and for me, the levels in this game doesn't feel as memorable as in the classic entries. Still, it's a fun and entertaining game with overwhelming SW content, but the level design of the originals still more legendary.

English Version (french below) : 

This is THE celebration of Star Wars. All 9 episodes, lots of different planets to go to, a crazy amount of characters with lots of them having their own idle animations and banters in combination with other characters, plenty of ships with cool space combat, missions and original Star Wars music, this game is full with content. 

And that sometimes is the problem with it. It's been a while since I completed it, but I do remember that there are lots of missions / bricks but that the diversity of environments does tend to make it better, but doing the main campaign, there is few actual levels for each episode (it's the price to pay to have all 9 of them) and there is quite a lot of walking to do between each section, which can get a bit annoying. 
Now, there is a skill tree for all classes but it's not really necessary. It's nice that it's there, but I personnally didn't use it that much. 

The combat system is nice, much deeper than it needed to be in a LEGO game but it's not an issue whatsoever.

I don't really have much more to say, if you're a fan of Star Wars, I think you will like it.




Version Française : 

C'est LA célébration de Star Wars. Les 9 épisodes, plein de planètes différentes à explorer, un nombre fou de personnages avec chacun leurs petites animations et leurs dialogues avec certains autres personnages, plein de vaisseaux avec des combats spatiaux bien sympa, de missions et de musiques originales de la Saga Star Wars, le jeu est plein à craquer de contenu.

Et c'est parfois ce qui peut lui poser problème. Ca fait un moment que je l'ai fini, mais je me souviens qu'il y avait vraiment beaucoup de missions / briques mais que la diversité des planètes aidait à le faire passer. Par contre pendant la campagne principale, il y a assez peu de niveaux dans chaque épisode (le prix à payer pour avoir les 9) and pas mal de marche entre différentes sections, ce qui peut être lourd. Il y a aussi des arbres d…

LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga is the biggest LEGO Star Wars game yet.
Exploring different planets is easily the best part of the game.
There’s a huge variety of locations, tons of characters, and endless reasons to wander off from the main story.

A fun and relaxing experience, the story sections are relatively short if you don't count the walk and talk, cutscenes are joyfully nostalgic. A big chunk of content in the game is the open world, which is beautiful and cool to explore for a while. If you were to do just that being the story and looking around, then your experience will be enjoyable if not a bit short. Going for 100% will take up around 80-90% of your time, since there are and absurd amount of collectibles and obvious time wasters to make the game seem larger than it is. You'll watch the landing sequence hundreds of times while jumping from system to system, just to talk to someone or deliver some vegetables. You'll do hundreds of puzzles, just to realize it's the same 4 or 5 puzzles just in a different place. The abilities in my opinion don't matter since it's a lego game and dying has no consequences anyways. The nonstop cantina music helps while doing the collectibles. If you like Star Wars and don't mind collectathons, then this is right up your alley.

TLDR : Fun if not excessively cluttered with timewasters.

citations.review_text:
[quote]TL;DR: Worth it for LEGO and Star Wars fans, but bugs may test your patience.[/quote]

I played LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga on PC (Linux via Proton) at ultra settings. No difficulty here, but plenty of chaos. I initially dropped it when the game crashed at 78% completion, wiping my save. Eventually, I restarted and logged about 120 hours. Some bugs forced hard restarts, like a character switch glitch that locked the game. But I loved the nods to the classic LEGO Star Wars games and the creative open-world tasks, collecting bricks felt genuinely rewarding. For the £24 I spent, the fun outweighed the frustration, but those bugs drop it to a 6/10.

So annoying. It randomly starts split-screen, and I can't disable it. Every second time I focus the game (tab out and back in), I get a white screen and have to refocus it again. The resolution randomly changes after minimizing the game...

Still no online co-op in lego games, and the camera in this title drives me crazy.
hard locked inside multiple levels, even more bugged with coop, how much levels i have to end because a boss fight is stuck or character cant be changed in free play when you need to use a specific one to progress the level. insane bugged, cant recommend, how often i  have to restart a level or the hole game because of bugs

This game was honestly fun at first. However once you play for awhile, you realize how flawed it is. There are way too many bugs and the fact the creators just gave up on it really sucks and kind of sours my taste for the company. They didn't even try to fix it. The gameplay is worse than any of the originals. What do i mean? Abilities for some of the characters are gone and replaced with class abilities. The levels were shortened which is a bummer. Each episode is just made worse thanks to them being shortened. They took away the coolest part of episode 3 and that's having u and your 2nd player fight each other as Anakin and Obi wan. This just feels like each game crammed together just to shorten the time it takes to make the game. No thought just make each game worse and put them together. Way too many loading screens thanks to constantly having to travel to different planets thanks to quests. Could have shortened bounty missions by just having us kill 30 ships instead of killing like 10 and having to teleport to the next area to kill 10 more. Sometimes the kyber brick detector wouldn't even work. Me and my coop had to restart levels many times thanks to bugs. Honestly the only thing they didn't butcher is the humor. I wouldn't recommend this game over the old ones. Just buy the older ones and play those. They actually feel like they cared back then with those games. 4/10 don't waste your money on this game

I enjoyed it, cpu performance can be very bad in some areas, I also experienced a fun bug where I could not redo hoth and cold, I kinda fixed it by replacing gameprogress.blob with one from a new save but that keeps track of what missions you have done in story mode

I'm having a lot of fun in this game. I was initially surprised at how different it was from TCS but its nice. voice acting is good and it follows the story pretty well. the game softlocks sometimes but its not a huge problem.

I was really excited to play this game, but by the time I had finished it I was relieved to uninstall it. This game was bloated and boring. The classic Lego game combat was tossed out in favor of a generic third person shooter combat system. The fun platforming and puzzles that have been a stable of these games was toned down and held my hand. Every platforming section is essentially a disguised quick time event that's hard to fail. And the "puzzles" were mostly just boring minigames. The levels were too short and each episode had only five levels instead of six, meaning some of the best parts of the movies didn't make it into the game proper. Not only were some mission in the previous Lego Star Wars games missing, but some others were replaced with worse alternatives. Many fun story beats which should have been in the game, and were in the previous games, were turned into walking segments in the open world. Meaning you can't replay those parts. And worse yet, some fun sections were just made into cutscenes. For example, the entire space battle of Endor consists of just a cutscene. I was looking forward to hearing movie dialogue in game similar to what I experienced with Lego Lord of the Rings, and was disappointed to find that was not the case and the voice actors were brought in instead. This is a nitpick on my part though, thankfully the voice acting was good even if it was unbearably corny. And while the story levels themselves suffered from being too short, the open world portion of the game suffered from being too long. This game has the highest number of collectibles I've encountered in a Lego game, and most of them involve boring radiant fetch quests which make the ones in Skyrim looks dynamic and fun by comparison. And many of these fetch quests will take you through several loading screens, or loading screens disguised as "immersive space travel" or a combination of both. They'll likely have at least one obligatory space dogfight which gets repetitive…

It's a Lego game, with all of the idiosyncrasies and baked-in gameplay elements that implies. TT has evolved the series over the years, mostly positively: the gun-handling in this one is smooth and feels more modern than previous games, for example. On the negative side, having actual understandable dialogue still feels wrong for a Lego game - the point didn't used to be "the player can follow the story and actually understand what's happening." (That may be my own grumpiness talking.)

Like all Lego games, it's full of collectibles (bricks, "datacards," characters, ships), unlocks based on collectibles, and sidebar content like races and what I have to call side-quests. Most of that is long-familiar from previous Lego games; the side-quests are newer. Main quests in this one are shorter and more focused than past games; I haven't gone back for free play yet, but I suspect that will make them more fun to re-play - not having to slog for half an hour to get one minikit at the end of a level.

This one has multiple hub locations, full of stuff - that's where, I think, most of the collectible-chasing actually happens, not in the main levels. That's a good shift: hub worlds are better-built for random futzing around to begin with.

I'm only maybe a third of the way through the game - less if you're counting up to 100%, like a lot of us Lego goofballs - but the changes TT has made are positive and tend to reinforce what's fun and distinctive about Lego games. I don't see Skywalker Saga changing the minds of players who don't like Lego games to begin with, but, for those that do, this is a modern, content-filled version of the thing we like, if slightly less goofy than the original versions.

Update at 110+ hours: Like a lot of Lego games, it gets more annoying as you chase the fiddly achievements and level challenges. The camera controls occasionally freak out when your character is too close to a wall. The prompts to use persona-specific abilities don't always appear wh…

Its a very polished and fun game. But the puzzles are basically non existent or very easy and the levels are very short. It's a different kind of game compared to the older Lego games with longer levels - keep that in mind.

It has a design much more akin to Super Mario Odyssey, where you go around these worlds and try and collect shiny Lego bricks. Not what I expected, but still fun.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that pursuing 100 percent completion involves a massive and repetitive grind.

citations.review_text:
I can't say that I didn't like this game. However, I did find it incredibly frustrating. 

It is beautiful and various mechanics are incredibly satisfying. A lot people suggest that this is missing the LEGO charm found in the older games, but I don't think that it's true. It is there, but it's buried by the grind and slog to 100% the game, making it's charm feel pretty fleeting. 

There are far too many collectibles in this game. I have just finished getting all the achievements, but it was an endeavour of diminishing returns. The universe is expansive but 1200 kyber bricks? Are you on crack? 

I did enjoy the game, but I am so happy I will never have to go through the grind again. 

I do recommend it, but I hope you're someone who is happy to leave things unfinished. You'll enjoy it more than I did.

I would recommend this game, BUT if you're trying to do a perfect game to get all achievements on Steam, you'd better be ready to freaking grind and grind some more. You MUST get Gold EVERYWHERE to get ALL you need. You also MUST do the WHOLE GAME and get perfect scores all the time. If you DON'T do this, forget about your perfect game! Their races in space are hell to play. They don't show you where to go, and getting the gold is extremely difficult. I must also add that this game runs REALLY well, there are no bugs or crashes, everything is smooth sailing, so a huge BRAVO for that! Finally, an immense congratulations to the team in charge of dialogue as it was impeccable, funny for both children and adults, and so well thought out! All in all, a great game!

If you want good LEGO Star Wars game, go play Lego Star Wars III.
Story is okay-ish (come on, everybody knows the story at this point, it's just lego-fied here), but challenges will make sure you will lose your psyche. It doesn't even bring anything significant in new mechanics compared to other and older LEGO games. 
You will skim through story line in maybe 10 hours and spend next 90 (or more, I used exploits and skips to get to Kyber Bricks) to make it 100%. A lot of puzzles to get Bricks is same, jump around, time trial, shoot targets. Very few puzzles are unique. Side quests are okay, unless it's escort mission. why, you may ask? Because NPCs move faster than your walk speed and slower than your sprint speed. Lovely, right? 
And there are also side quests requiring moving through half of galaxy. Talk with one guy, go to another planet, talk with another guy, hunt something, pack your ship and come back to first guy, occasionally forcing out of hyperspace to engage in annoying fight with groups of enemy fighters. 

Overall, game is not some massive upgrade over other games, it has TON of grinding, a lot of stuff is repetitive, making whole experience boring. Can't recommend.
